rules.title: Security Deposit Return for Domestic Violence Lease Termination
rules.quote: Within 15 business days after the lease is terminated, the landlord shall make available the return of the tenant's security deposit, plus any interest earned, to the tenant or the tenant's agent.
rules.summary: When a tenant terminates a lease due to domestic violence under the Safe Housing Act, the landlord must return the security deposit plus interest within 15 business days.
rules.exemption_note: Does not apply to transient or seasonal rentals

rules.title: Security Deposit Return for Service Members
rules.quote: The landlord is required to return the security deposit in accordance with the applicable Security Deposit Law (N.J.S.A. 46:8-26).
rules.summary: Service members who terminate their lease under the Service Members Civil Relief Act are entitled to return of their security deposit under New Jersey's Security Deposit Law.

rules.title: Dishonored Payment Fees
rules.quote: Dishonored payment fees (N.J.S.A. 2A:32A-1)
rules.summary: Landlords may charge dishonored payment fees as authorized by statute.

rules.title: Service or Guide Dog Accommodation Requirement
rules.quote: A handicapped, blind, or deaf person who has a service or guide dog, or who obtains a service or guide dog, shall have full and equal access to all housing accommodations and shall not be required to pay extra compensation. Any lease or rental agreement prohibiting pets shall not apply to a service or guide dog owned by a handicapped, blind, or deaf tenant.
rules.summary: Landlords cannot discriminate against handicapped, blind, or deaf tenants who have service or guide dogs, and no-pet clauses do not apply to service or guide dogs.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act - Good Cause Requirement
rules.quote: No landlord of residential rental properties except those in owner occupied two or three family dwellings, motels or hotels, transient, or seasonal units may fail to renew any lease, regardless of whether it is written or oral unless they have good cause not to renew the lease.
rules.summary: Landlords of most residential rental properties cannot refuse to renew a lease or evict tenants without good cause as defined by law.
rules.coverage_text: Except those in owner occupied two or three family dwellings, motels or hotels, transient, or seasonal units
rules.exemption_note: Does not apply to owner-occupied two or three family dwellings, motels, hotels, transient or seasonal units

rules.title: Late Fee Requirements - Senior Citizen Grace Period
rules.quote: There is a five (5) 'business day' grace period for senior citizens before a late fee may be assessed. A business day does not include Saturday, Sunday, State or Federal holidays.
rules.summary: Senior citizen tenants are entitled to a five business day grace period before late fees can be charged on rent.

rules.title: Maximum Security Deposit Limit
rules.quote: The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than one and one-half times one month's rent
rules.summary: A landlord cannot collect a security deposit that exceeds one and one-half times one month's rent.
rules.coverage_text: The Security Deposit Law applies to most residential rental properties, including mobile homes. The exception is an owner-occupied two-, or three-family dwelling.
rules.exemption_note: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are exempt unless tenant requests in writing that landlord follow Security Deposit Law requirements.

rules.title: Security Deposit Return Deadline
rules.quote: Within 30 days after the termination of a tenancy, a landlord must return the security deposit, plus interest earned less deductions, to the tenant
rules.summary: The landlord must return the security deposit plus interest, minus any lawful deductions, within 30 days after the tenancy ends.
rules.coverage_text: The Security Deposit Law applies to most residential rental properties, including mobile homes. The exception is an owner-occupied two-, or three-family dwelling.
rules.exemption_note: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are exempt unless tenant requests in writing that landlord follow Security Deposit Law requirements.
rules.penalty: If a landlord fails to return the security deposit within 30 days, or the tenant disagrees with the amount deducted, the tenant may sue for double the amount of the security deposit that the tenant contends was wrongfully withheld, together with court costs and reasonable attorney's fees.

rules.title: Security Deposit Interest Payment
rules.quote: The interest or earnings paid on the security deposit belongs to the tenant and shall be paid to the tenant in cash or credited toward rent due and owing on the renewal or anniversary of the tenant's lease or on January 31
rules.summary: Interest earned on security deposits belongs to the tenant and must be paid annually at lease renewal, anniversary, or on January 31.
rules.coverage_text: The Security Deposit Law applies to most residential rental properties, including mobile homes. The exception is an owner-occupied two-, or three-family dwelling.
rules.exemption_note: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are exempt unless tenant requests in writing that landlord follow Security Deposit Law requirements.

rules.title: Security Deposit Wrongful Withholding for Subsidized Tenants
rules.quote: Any landlord who willfully and intentionally withholds a security deposit made by or on behalf of a tenant who has received financial assistance through any State or federal program, including welfare or rental assistance, may be penalized. The landlord may be liable for a civil penalty of not less than $500 or not more than $2,000 for each offense.
rules.summary: A landlord who willfully withholds a security deposit from a tenant receiving government assistance may face a civil penalty of $500 to $2,000 per offense.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to tenants who have received financial assistance through any State or federal program, including welfare or rental assistance.
rules.penalty: Civil penalty of not less than $500 or not more than $2,000 for each offense, collected by summary proceedings pursuant to the Penalty Enforcement Law (N.J.S.A. 2A:58-12).

rules.title: Source of Income Discrimination Prohibition
rules.quote: The New Jersey Law Against Discrimination (LAD), N.J.S.A. 10:5-12(g) to -(h), prohibits discrimination when selling or renting property and requires equal treatment in the sale or rental of housing regardless of race, creed, color, national origin, ancestry, sex, marital status, civil union status, domestic partnership status, familial status, affectional or sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, mental and physical disability, nationality, or source of lawful income.
rules.summary: Landlords cannot discriminate in renting based on source of lawful income, among other protected classes.
rules.coverage_text: The law applies to all landlord-tenant relationships, except those involving two-family owner occupied dwellings, rooms in an owner or resident-occupied single home, and residences planned exclusively for and occupied by one sex.
rules.exemption_note: Two-family owner occupied dwellings, rooms in an owner or resident-occupied single home, and residences planned exclusively for and occupied by one sex (e.g. YMCA) are exempt, as well as age-restricted housing as it pertains to familial status.
rules.penalty: Landlords who violate this law are subject to substantial fines and penalties, up to $10,000 for a first offense (N.J.S.A. 10:5-14.1a(a)).

rules.title: Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Rent Control Exemption
rules.quote: Under the Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Law (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5), newly constructed multiple dwellings shall be exempt from any local rent control ordinances for a period of 30 years following completion of construction of the building.
rules.summary: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from local rent control ordinances for 30 years after construction is completed.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to newly constructed multiple dwellings.
rules.exemption_note: This exemption applies to newly constructed multiple dwellings for 30 years following completion of construction.

rules.title: Registration required before eviction - 1-2 family non-owner-occupied
rules.quote: The landlord registration law prohibits a landlord from evicting a tenant in the building if the landlord has not been properly registered (N.J.S.A. 46:8-27 to -37).
rules.summary: A landlord who owns a one or two-family non-owner-occupied home cannot evict a tenant unless the landlord has been properly registered with the municipality or Bureau of Housing Inspection.
rules.exemption_note: Owner-occupied two-family homes are not required to be registered and thus exempt from this restriction.

rules.title: Registration required before eviction - 3+ units
rules.quote: If the building has three (3) or more units, the statement must be filed with the Bureau of Housing Inspection, Post Office Box 810, Trenton, New Jersey 08625-0810, on a registration form provided by the Bureau. The landlord registration law prohibits a landlord from evicting a tenant in the building if the landlord has not been properly registered (N.J.S.A. 46:8-27 to -37).
rules.summary: A landlord who owns a building with three or more units cannot evict a tenant unless the landlord has been properly registered with the Bureau of Housing Inspection.
rules.coverage_text: building has three (3) or more units

rules.title: Good cause required for eviction
rules.quote: A landlord may recover possession of a dwelling unit used as a residence only by consent of the tenants or through the legal process of eviction. A landlord must have good cause to evict a tenant (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-53). No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause.
rules.summary: A landlord must have good cause to evict a tenant or to fail to renew a lease, and can only recover possession through the tenant's consent or the legal eviction process.
rules.coverage_text: dwelling unit used as a residence

rules.title: Good Cause Eviction Required Under Anti-Eviction Act
rules.quote: Listed below are the statutory grounds for eviction as set forth in the Anti-Eviction Statute. A. Failure to Pay Rent If a tenant fails to pay rent, the landlord may immediately take legal action to have the tenant evicted.
rules.summary: Landlords may evict tenants only for causes listed in the Anti-Eviction Act, including failure to pay rent, disorderly conduct, property damage, lease violations, and other specified statutory grounds.
rules.coverage_text: The Anti-Eviction Act applies to most residential rental properties including single-family homes, mobile homes and land in a mobile home park, apartment buildings, and complexes.
rules.exemption_note: May not apply to two- or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units.

rules.title: Relocation Assistance Required for Health and Safety or Removal from Rental Market Evictions
rules.quote: Tenants evicted under this cause may be eligible for financial and other assistance for relocation. If eligible, this assistance must be provided before the tenant can be evicted.
rules.summary: Tenants evicted due to health and safety violations or permanent removal from the rental market must receive relocation assistance before they can be evicted.

rules.title: Relocation Assistance for Illegal Occupancy Evictions
rules.quote: Any tenant evicted under G 3) (illegal occupancy) is entitled to relocation assistance in an amount equal to six times the tenant's monthly rent. The landlord is responsible for paying the tenant's relocation expenses.
rules.summary: Tenants evicted due to illegal occupancy must receive relocation assistance equal to six times the monthly rent, paid by the landlord at least five days before removal.
rules.penalty: If landlord does not pay within required time, interest accrues at 18% per year; amount due is a lien on the property.

rules.title: Penalties for Wrongful Personal Occupancy Eviction
rules.quote: When a tenant vacates a dwelling unit after having been given notice that the landlord wishes to personally occupy the unit the landlord must occupy the unit for at least six (6) months. If instead the landlord permits personal occupancy of the unit by another tenant or registration of conversion of the property to a condominium or cooperative, the landlord is liable to the former tenant for three (3) times the damages suffered plus attorney fees and costs
rules.summary: If a landlord evicts a tenant for personal occupancy but fails to occupy the unit for at least six months, the landlord must pay the former tenant three times the damages plus attorney fees and costs.
rules.penalty: Three times the damages suffered plus attorney fees and costs

rules.title: Penalties for Wrongful Permanent Retirement Eviction
rules.quote: When a tenant vacates a dwelling unit after having been given notice that the landlord seeks to permanently board up or demolish the building or to permanently retire it from residential use, the landlord must not use this property for residential use for a period of five (5) years. If the landlord allows any residential use of the unit during the five (5) year period from the date the unit became vacant, the landlord, or the former landlord, may be liable to the tenant for three (3) times the damages plus attorney fees and costs. Additionally, the landlord or former landlord may be liable for a civil penalty up to $10,000.00 for each violation
rules.summary: If a landlord evicts a tenant for permanent retirement from residential use but uses the property residentially within five years, the landlord must pay three times damages plus attorney fees and costs, and may face a civil penalty up to $10,000 per violation.
rules.penalty: Three times the damages plus attorney fees and costs; civil penalty up to $10,000.00 per violation

rules.title: Anti-Retaliation Protection for Tenant Rights
rules.quote: A landlord cannot take reprisal action against a tenant by eviction, substantial alteration of a lease or its terms, or refusal to renew a lease when a tenant exercises certain civil rights
rules.summary: Landlords cannot evict, substantially alter lease terms, or refuse to renew a lease in retaliation for a tenant exercising civil rights, including enforcing lease rights, making good faith complaints to authorities, organizing with other tenants, or refusing lease changes made in retaliation.
rules.coverage_text: The law against reprisal applies to all rental properties used for dwelling purposes, including mobile homes, except owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings.
rules.exemption_note: Except owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings
rules.penalty: Tenant may sue the landlord for damages in a civil action

rules.title: Foreclosure Tenant Protection - 90 Day Notice Required
rules.quote: Before a tenant can be evicted due to foreclosure, the landlord must provide the tenant with a 90-day notice to quit when the foreclosed property has been purchased by a buyer who wants to personally occupy it as his or her primary residence. However, if a tenant has a lease agreement that goes beyond the 90 days the landlord may not take action to evict the tenant until after the lease expires and the 90-day notice to quit has been given.
rules.summary: Tenants in foreclosed properties must receive a 90-day notice to quit if a buyer wants to personally occupy the property, and existing leases must be honored through their term before eviction can proceed.
rules.coverage_text: Month-to-month tenants and two- and three-family owner-occupied units are not exempt from the 90-day notice requirements.

rules.title: Ban on Self-Help Evictions and Lockouts
rules.quote: A landlord or any other person who enters an apartment or property without a court order authorizing such entry and/or holds a tenant's belongings unlawfully by force or threat of monies owed may be liable for damages to the tenant
rules.summary: Self-help evictions and lockouts—entering a unit to remove tenants or their belongings without a court order, or disconnecting utilities to force a tenant out—are illegal, and landlords may be liable for damages.
rules.penalty: Liable for damages to the tenant; may be charged with disorderly conduct; court may award possession, all damages, court costs and reasonable attorney fees
